clue.text: Goes on about drugs during reminder to son

indicators.note: something happening during something else sits inside it, so these letters go within the next ones

parts.note: a prod is a nudge that reminds someone
C is short for circa, about
E is ecstasy, so two of them make drugs
S is the usual abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone rambles on about drugs while giving their son a reminder.
explanation.walkthrough: Two drugs because E, ecstasy, is doubled for the plural; about as C is the Latin circa, seen in dates.
explanation.definitionFit: To proceed is to continue or carry on, so proceeds is a synonym of goes on.

clue.text: Essentially accurate about the German being more robust

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the kept letters are read backwards
the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are wanted

parts.note: the two central letters of this eight-letter word
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German is described as basically accurate and sturdier than others.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruder here is the old sense of rude, sturdy or vigorous, as in the phrase rude health, not impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean vigorous and hearty, as in the idiom rude health, so ruder means sturdier or more robust.

clue.text: Consider making changes in it free to copy

indicators.note: changes made to a group of letters rearrange them into a new order

parts.note: to count someone lucky is to consider them so
these six letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about altering a document so that it can be copied freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To counterfeit is to forge or imitate something, such as money, so it means to copy fraudulently.

clue.text: Occurring again and again over vote involving foreign nations

indicators.note: one thing laid over another covers it, so these letters wrap around the next

parts.note: eternal can mean incessant, constantly recurring
a cross is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A recurring vote on matters concerning other countries, like a perpetual referendum.
explanation.walkthrough: The ballot cross sits inside ETERNAL, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: External affairs are a country's dealings with other states, so external means relating to foreign countries.

clue.text: Immediately getting 1 of 19 for Frank

parts.note: straight away or straight off means immediately
the answer at 19 is plural, so one of them is singular

explanation.surface: Someone instantly gets one of a set of things in exchange for a man called Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 19-across is FORWARDS; one of them is a single FORWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A straightforward person is honest and open, so the word is a synonym of frank.

clue.text: Influenced unfairly by Poins when involved in plot

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so these letters go within the next

parts.note: a flower bed is a garden plot
Poins is the setter, who refers to himself as I
as can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: The setter admits being partial when he was mixed up in a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: I and AS go inside B-ED, giving B-I-AS-ED. A setter's own pseudonym in a clue usually stands for I or ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Biased means prejudiced, having one's judgement swayed unfairly towards one side.

clue.text: Clergyman's book is hard work

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
taken as written
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A churchman complains that his book was difficult to write.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Clergyman's reads as is, joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a senior member of the clergy in charge of a diocese.

clue.text: Foolhardy rector missing in wood

indicators.note: something missing has been taken away, so these letters lose one

parts.note: rash means reckless
R is the abbreviation for rector

explanation.surface: A reckless clergyman has gone missing in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R away from RASH to leave ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a tree and also its timber, so it is an example of wood.

clue.text: Used former policeman to carry it to Spain

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so the next letters go inside

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, so ex means former
plod is British slang for a police officer, from Mr Plod in the Noddy books
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A retired officer was made use of to take something over to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Plod is British slang for a police officer, from PC Plod in the Noddy children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit someone is to use them unfairly for one's own ends, so exploited means used.

clue.text: Alter notice in accordance with facts

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a public notice
just can mean correct, well founded on fact

explanation.surface: Someone is told to amend a notice so it agrees with the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust something is to change it slightly, so it is a synonym of alter.

clue.text: Girl's covering body part with fruit

indicators.note: a covering goes all around what it covers, so these letters wrap the next

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name; the possessive adds S
the hip is a part of the body

explanation.surface: A young woman hides part of her body behind some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive Girl's supplies the final S, so the body part sits between the name and that S.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosehips are the red berries left on a rose bush, used for syrup, so they are a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Revolutionary measure to imprison royalist leader

indicators.note: imprisoning someone shuts them inside, so the next letter goes within these

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A political measure is proposed to jail the head of the monarchist faction.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutionary here is a noun: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a follower of the revolutionary Leon Trotsky.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trot is a Trotskyist, an adherent of permanent revolution, so the slang word names a revolutionary.

clue.text: Horny type getting hornier frolicking outside club with sailor

indicators.note: frolicking is playing about wildly, so these letters romp into a new order
something outside another surrounds it, so the jumbled letters wrap the next one

parts.note: these seven letters rearranged
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
OS stands for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A randy fellow gets randier larking about outside a nightclub with a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Horny looks like slang for lustful, but the definition means literally having a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinoceros is the animal famous for the horn on its snout, so it is a creature with horns.

clue.text: Mark follows it with an excited cry

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word that comes before mark in the name of the punctuation symbol !
second meaning: a sudden emotional shout

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark trails along behind, shouting excitedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a person's name, but it is the word mark in the phrase for the ! symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The ! sign is called an exclamation mark, and an exclamation is also a sudden outcry of emotion.

clue.text: Come close to making an initial proposal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to draw near to something
second meaning: to sound someone out with a first offer

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idea about nearly proposing, but it is two separate senses of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: You approach a place by moving nearer, and you approach a person when you first put an offer or request to them.

clue.text: Severely criticise having old theatrical technique propping up Travers' earliest farce

indicators.note: in a down answer, what props something up sits beneath it, so the following letters come after

parts.note: critics pan a show they hate

indicators.note: the earliest part of a word is its beginning, so only its first letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter of the name
O is the abbreviation for old
mime is acting by gesture without words

explanation.surface: A critic savages a dated stage style that underpins one of Ben Travers' farces.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Travers was an English playwright famed for the Aldwych farces. A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show for families, full of slapstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime can mean an absurd or chaotic situation, a farce, besides the slapstick Christmas show.

clue.text: Charlotte, for instance, is extremely coy about exactly what's needed

indicators.note: about here means around, so the kept letters surround the next ones
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of this word
it can mean the very thing, as in that's it

explanation.surface: A woman called Charlotte is very shy about precisely what she requires.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlotte looks like a woman's name, but it is the city in North Carolina.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte in North Carolina is a large US city, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Overweening republican seen in old marketplace returning books

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the letters are read in reverse
to be seen in a place is to be inside it, so this letter goes within the next ones

parts.note: the agora was the public square and market of an ancient Greek city
R is the abbreviation for republican
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A pompous republican is spotted in an ancient market bringing back some books.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into AGORA to make AGORRA, which reversed gives ARROGA; NT completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overweening means excessively proud and presumptuous, which is what an arrogant person is.

clue.text: Some of grant earmarked for advance payment

indicators.note: only some of the following words are used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Part of a grant has been set aside for paying in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake a poker player puts in before the deal, a payment made in advance.

clue.text: Ahead of the pack

parts.note: surface reading: leading the field, out in front of the rest; setter's reading: in rugby the pack is the group of players who scrum down, and ahead means onward

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the pack is made up of the forward players; the answer also means onward or ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means towards the front, and rugby's forwards are the players who make up the scrum pack.

clue.text: Vehicle parked in the London area by day is alarmed

indicators.note: a vehicle parked in a place sits within it, so these letters go inside the next

parts.note: SE is the London postcode area, south-east
a car is a vehicle
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A driver who left their car in London overnight is worried about it.
explanation.walkthrough: SE is the south-east London postcode district, a common crossword stand-in for London.
explanation.definitionFit: Scared means frightened, which is what someone alarmed feels.

clue.text: Clare and Tom on jaunt in town

indicators.note: a jaunt is an outing, so the letters take a trip into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple, Clare and Tom, go off on a trip to some town.
explanation.walkthrough: Monte Carlo is the resort town of Monaco, famous for its casino.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo is a resort district of Monaco, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: It's found in Castilian wine

indicators.note: something found in another is tucked inside it, so the letters lie within the next word

parts.note: letters two to five of this word

explanation.surface: A claim that something is present in a Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Castilian suggests a Spanish wine, but the answer is Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in north-west Italy.

clue.text: Thanks primarily to Bill it's understood

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the word's first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
AC, short for account, is a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gratitude goes mainly to a man called Bill, and that goes without saying.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name; it is an account. The ‘s of it's is read as is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied without being stated, so a tacit agreement is understood rather than spoken.

clue.text: Itinerant vicar to go around island in carriage

indicators.note: going around something encircles it, so the jumbled letters enclose the next one

parts.note: these seven letters rearranged
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A travelling clergyman tours an island in a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A victoria is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage named after Queen Victoria.

clue.text: An article of faith eventually embraced by Taiwanese extremists

indicators.note: to be embraced is to be held within arms, so this letter goes inside the next ones

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only its first and last letters count

parts.note: the final letter of this word; the answer also happens to run across faith eventually, a coincidence

explanation.walkthrough: Article of faith reads as one phrase meaning a firm belief; the definition is just An article.

clue.text: Answer with an example of each

explanation.walkthrough: With is a joining word here: A goes with PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for or to each one, as in a pound apiece.

clue.text: Posh girl sent back to finish story

the end is the finish

explanation.walkthrough: Gel imitates the upper-class British pronunciation of girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale handed down, often about heroes, so it is a kind of story.

clue.text: Set off with volunteers well known around the centre of Leeds

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the preceding letters run backwards

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force
noted means famous

parts.note: the third of this word's five letters

explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off, making it explode.
